questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 10 km/h. The speed of the stream is 2 km/h. What is the total distance that the boat will travel if it is rowed for 4 hours upstream and 3 hours downstream?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Upstream Speed = 10 − 2 = 8 km/h and Downstream Speed = 10 + 2 = 12 km/h.

Total Distance = (Upstream Speed × Upstream Time) + (Downstream Speed × Downstream Time)

Total Distance = (8 × 4) + (12 × 3) = 32 + 36 = 68 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 68 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Speed of boat in still water = 10 km/h

⇒ Speed of stream = 2 km/h

⇒ Time taken upstream = 4 hours

⇒ Time taken downstream = 3 hours

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/421ef4c156cf160ba0631e9603c7994de03f2e4e95c6158f4581cc178ee00e3c.png] 

**Formulas Used:**

⇒ Upstream Speed = Speed of boat − Speed of stream

⇒ Downstream Speed = Speed of boat + Speed of stream

⇒ Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Upstream Speed = 10 − 2 = 8 km/h

⇒ Downstream Speed = 10 + 2 = 12 km/h

⇒ Distance traveled upstream = 8 × 4 = 32 km

⇒ Distance traveled downstream = 12 × 3 = 36 km

⇒ Total Distance = 32 + 36 = 68 km

**∴ The correct answer is 68 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed of Boat in Still Water

If downstream and upstream speeds are given, then Boat Speed = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Speed of Stream

If downstream and upstream speeds are given, then Stream Speed = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Average Speed for Equal Distances

If a boat travels equal distances upstream and downstream, the Average Speed = (Upstream Speed × Downstream Speed) ÷ Boat Speed in still water.

questions.question: Ratio of the number of sides of two regular polygons is 5 : 6 and the ratio of their each interior angle is 24 : 25. Then the number of sides of these two polygons are
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ratio of the number of sides of two regular polygons = 5 : 6

Ratio of each interior angle = 24 : 25

**Concept used:**

For any regular polygon, Interior angle + Exterior angle = 180°

Each exterior angle = 360°/n

Each interior angle = {(n - 2) × 180°}/n

Where n = number of sides of the regular polygon 

**Calculation:**

Let the number of sides be 5x and 6x respectively. Then,

{(5x - 2) × 180°/5x}/{(6x - 2) × 180°/6x} = 24/25

⇒ {6 × (5x - 2)}/{5 × (6x - 2)} = 24/25

⇒ (5x - 2)/(6x - 2) = (5 × 24)/ (6 ×25) = 4/5

⇒ x = 2

∴ 5x = 5 × 2 = 10 and 6x = 6 × 2 = 12

**∴ The number of sides of the two polygons be 10 and 12**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**For any regular polygon of n number of sides 

Exterior angle = 360°/n

Interior angle + Exterior angle = 180° 

Internal angle = 180° - Exterior angle 

⇒ Internal angle = 180° - 360°/n

Therefore according to the question,

{180º – (360º/5x)}/{180º – (360 º/6x)} = 24/25

{180º (5x – 2)/5x} × {6x/360º (3x – 1)} = 24 / 25

75x – 30 = 72x – 24

⇒ 3x = 6 ⇒ x = 2

∴ 5x = 5 × 2 = 10 and 6x = 6 × 2 = 12

**∴ The number of sides of the two polygons be 10 and 12**

questions.question: If the length of a rectangle is increased by 11.11 percent, then by how much percentage its breadth should be reduced to keep the area same?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of rectangle increases by 11.11%

**Formula used:**

Area = Length × Breadth

**Calculations:**

Let the initial length be L and initial breadth be B.

New length = L × (1 + 11.11/100) = L × 1.1111

To keep the area constant, New Area = Old Area

⇒ L × B = (L × 1.1111) × (B - x%)

⇒ B = (1.1111 × (B - x%))

⇒ 1 = 1.1111 - (x% × 1.1111)

⇒ x% = 1 - 1/1.1111

⇒ x% = 0.1111

⇒ x% = 10%

**∴ The breadth should be reduced by 10% to keep the area the same.**

questions.question: A 21 m high flag post is cut in such a way that its top touches the ground and makes an angle of 30° with the ground. At what height form the bottom is the post cut?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a 30°-60°-90° right-angled triangle, the opposite sides are in the ratio 1 : √3 : 2.

The perpendicular (height of the remaining post) corresponds to 1 part.

The hypotenuse (broken part of the post) corresponds to 2 parts.

Total height of the flag post = 1 part + 2 parts = 3 parts.

3 parts = 21 m ⇒ 1 part = 21 ÷ 3 = 7 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 7 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/921332dbe655728f1663224aae8736903933844fc47fe126a089c2ab0743801e.png] 

**Given:**

Total height of the flag post = 21 m

Angle of elevation made by the broken part with the ground = 30°

**Formula Used:**

sin(θ) = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse

**Calculations:**

Let the height from the bottom where the post is cut be x m.

Length of the broken top part that forms the hypotenuse = (21 − x) m.

In the right-angled triangle formed,

⇒ sin(30°) = x ÷ (21 − x)

⇒ 1 ÷ 2 = x ÷ (21 − x)

⇒ 21 − x = 2x

⇒ 3x = 21

⇒ x = 7 m

**∴ The correct answer is 7 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle of Elevation vs Depression

The angle of elevation is measured upwards from the horizontal line of sight, whereas the angle of depression is measured downwards. In alternate interior configurations, these two angles are equal.

For Amit: Work = 3 × (D - 32) = 3D - 96 units.

questions.question: In a group of 32 students, the average weight was 18.5 kg. When 4 students left the group, the average came down to 15.5 kg. What was the average weight (in kg) of those 4 students?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Decrease in average weight of remaining 28 students = 18.5 − 15.5 = 3 kg.

Total weight lost by these 28 students = 28 × 3 = 84 kg.

This means the 4 students took their own average share plus this lost weight.

Total weight of 4 students = (4 × 18.5) + 84 = 74 + 84 = 158 kg.

Average weight of these 4 students = 158 ÷ 4 = 39.5 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 39.5 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial students = 32, Initial average = 18.5 kg

Students remaining = 32 − 4 = 28, New average = 15.5 kg

**Formula Used:**

Total Weight = Average × Number of Students

Average of left students = Total weight of left students ÷ Number of left students

 
 Total Weight = 32 × 18.5 = 592 kg
 32 students, Average = 18.5 kg

 

 

 

 
 28 students, Avg = 15.5 kg
 Weight = 28 × 15.5 = 434 kg

 ∴ Average of 4 = 158 ÷ 4 = 39.5 kg

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total weight of 32 students = 32 × 18.5 = 592 kg

⇒ Total weight of remaining 28 students = 28 × 15.5 = 434 kg

⇒ Total weight of the 4 students who left = 592 − 434 = 158 kg

⇒ Average weight of the 4 students = 158 ÷ 4 = 39.5 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 39.5 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

If group A has n₁ elements with average A₁ and group B has n₂ elements with average A₂, then the combined average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Net Deviation Method

The sum of deviations of all observations from their actual average is always zero. This property is highly useful to rapidly find the value of included or excluded terms without complex multiplications.

Excluding a Member

If a member leaves and the average decreases, the leaving member's value is greater than the initial average: Left Value = Old Avg + (Decrease in Avg × Remaining Members).

__
 
• The given sentence is in active voice and uses the modal verb "**might**," so the passive voice must also use the modal verb "**might**."
 
• In the passive voice, the object of the active voice becomes the subject, and the subject becomes the agent.
 
• The passive voice with "might" is constructed by using **"might" + "be" + the past participle of the main verb.**

• Active Voice

 
 
• When an action performed by the subject is expressed by the verb, it is an active voice.
 
• Active voice is used when more straightforward relation and clarity is required between the subject and the verb.
 
 
• For example,
 
 
• Hens lay eggs.
 
• Birds build nests.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• Passive Voice
 
 
• When the action expressed by the verb is received by the subject, it is passive voice.
 
• Passive voice is used when the doer of the action is not known and the focus of the sentence is on the action and not the subject.
 
 
• For example,
 
 
• Eggs are laid by hens.
 
• Nests are built by birds.

questions.question: The Meissner effect is a defining characteristic of which state of matter?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Superconducting state**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Meissner effect** is the phenomenon where a material expels **magnetic fields** when it transitions into the **superconducting state**.
 
• This effect is a defining characteristic of superconductors and demonstrates their ability to exhibit **perfect diamagnetism**.
 
• In the superconducting state, the material's resistance drops to **zero**, allowing electric currents to flow without energy loss.
 
• The effect was discovered in **1933** by Walther Meissner and Robert Ochsenfeld.
 
• It occurs due to the formation of **Cooper pairs**, which are paired electrons that move without scattering.
 
• The Meissner effect is observed below a critical temperature, which varies depending on the type of superconducting material.
 
• The effect is utilized in technologies such as **magnetic levitation** and highly efficient electrical systems.
 
• Superconductors are categorized into two types: **Type I** and **Type II**, both exhibiting the Meissner effect but with different behaviors in external magnetic fields.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Paramagnetic state**__

 __
 
• In the **paramagnetic state**, materials are weakly attracted to external magnetic fields due to the alignment of magnetic moments.
 
• Unlike the superconducting state, paramagnetic materials do not exhibit **zero resistance** or expulsion of magnetic fields.
 
• Examples of paramagnetic materials include **aluminum**, **platinum**, and **magnesium.**
 
 
 
• **Ferromagnetic state**__
 __
 
• In the **ferromagnetic state**, materials exhibit strong attraction to magnetic fields and retain their magnetization even after the external field is removed.
 
• Examples include **iron**, **nickel**, and **cobalt**.
 
• Ferromagnetic materials are used in applications like **electric motors**, **transformers**, and **permanent magnets**.
 
 
 
• **Insulating state**__
 
 
• In the **insulating state**, materials do not conduct electricity due to the absence of free electrons or charge carriers.
 
• Common examples include **rubber**, **glass**, and **ceramics**.
 
• Insulators are widely used in **electrical wiring** and **circuit components** to prevent current leakage.

• **Square Plan of Nagara Temple Architecture**

 
 
• The basic plan of the Nagara temple architecture is square.
 
• Nagara style is one of the three main styles of temple architecture in India, primarily found in Northern India.
 
• The primary characteristic of the Nagara style is its square sanctum (garbhagriha), which houses the main deity.
 
• The square plan allows for clear axial alignment, often featuring a straight-line layout from the entrance to the sanctum.
 
• The shikhara (tower or spire) in Nagara architecture rises directly above the sanctum, emphasizing verticality.

• Nagara temples are often built on a raised platform called jagati.
 
• The temples frequently feature intricate carvings and sculptures, depicting deities, mythological scenes, and floral motifs.
 
• Examples of Nagara style temples include the Kandariya Mahadeva Temple in Khajuraho and the Sun Temple in Modhera.
 
 
 
• **Other Options**
 
 
• **Octagonal:** This is not a characteristic plan of Nagara architecture but can be found in some other architectural styles.
 
• **Rectangular:** Rectangular plans are more common in Dravidian temple architecture, prevalent in Southern India.
 
• **Round:** Circular or round plans are rare in Indian temple architecture and are not associated with the Nagara style.
